Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection of Chesapeake's Covington well site located in Sheshequin Township, Bradford County on 10/21/2021 at 1135 hours. The weather was 68 degrees with cloudy skies. The act 9 sign, site plans and onsite inspection log were all located at the entrance to the site. The inspection was conducted to follow-up on site conditions after a release of produced water to the pad surface was discovered on 9/14/2021. Production of the Covington 5H well has been temporarily ceased in order to remove production equipment and perform excavation activities. As of today, the majority of the excavation appears to have been completed and the pad has been regraded. The area of the discovered release is shown in photo #6. Excavated material has been placed on large secondary containment structures along the northern edge of the pad (photo #4). Some of the excavated material has been covered in addition to the secondary containment. All pooled water and damp soils that were field measured today were found to be low in electrical conductivity. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed onsite. Post-construction stormwater management controls have been installed and are functioning as designed. The large secondary containment structures appear to be functioning as designed. Violations cited against API # 015-21152 on 9/14/2021 remain outstanding at this time. Upon attainment with Act 2 standards, the violations could then be closed. No additional violations noted today. I departed the site at 1230 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-14
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 852794
Permit API: 117-21998
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-06-14
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess conditions on and off the pad. Both the 2H and 4H wells continue to flow back. A puddle in front of the west containment next to the MASS had a conductivity of 16.6 mS/cm. Another puddle to the south, not directly in front of the containment, had a conductivity of 4.96 mS/cm. Soil conductivity readings in this area ranged from 1.3 to >4 mS/cm when measured with the soil conductivity meter. On the main pad surface, the conductivity of puddles on the surface near the gravel piles remains elevated with conductivities above 2 mS/cm here. The area between the well heads, which had elevated conductivities during the previous inspection, has been back-filled with new gravel. After speaking with Taylor Parsons of Falcon on site about my conductivity readings, he accompanied me to the MASS. I showed him that the Oakton conductivity meter was showing that the puddles in front and to the south of the west containment were elevated. I took a conductivity reading of the fluid inside the containment which was >19.99 mS/cm. He stated that the containment may not be adequate for preventing spills of produced water to the surface when water trucks are off-loading the MASS. He said that he would have a more substantial area of containment built which would allow the trucks to drive onto the containment, which he believed would prevent produced water from getting onto the surface of the MASS pad. A contractor, Blood Hound, was on site when I arrived. The contractor marked the location of the PVC Pipe with spray paint and flags. The path is included as a red line in the map in photo #3. The attached maps and tables show the conductivity readings recorded during this inspection. Outstanding violations.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/22/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in Cascade Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/22/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 911116
Permit API: 081-21802
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/22/2021
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that produced water was released from a GPU dump line. The report stated that on Saturday, March 20, 2021, a crew monitoring the wells remotely noticed erratic gauge trends and the volume of the release was initially estimated at 1 to 5 barrels in this notification. I met with ARD representative Rick Hall on location. Mr. Hall told me that a failed valve on the 10H well GPU led to a release of 12 barrels of produced water to the pad surface. He said that they believe that the GPU dump line sprayed produced water inside the double-walled GPU for 2 hours and since the well produces an average of 12 barrels of produced water per hour, the total volume released from the line was 24 barrels. The containment within the GPU held 12 barrels of produced water and 12 barrels overflowed to the pad surface. The 10H well was remotely shut-in after two hours of erratic gauge trends. Mr. Hall stated that ARD intends to pursue Act 2 remediation and they contracted an environmental consultant, GES, to oversee the process. A line of puddles is present along the west edge of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of these puddles is 8.35 mS/cm in the area closest to the 10H GPU and the EC in the puddles decreases steadily farther away. The GPU was moved to another area of the pad and in the small puddle on the pad where it had been staged, the EC was greater than 19.99 mS/cm. When I relayed my findings to Mr. Hall, he stated that on Saturday morning, the puddles along the west side of the pad were all below 1 mS/cm. I took a sample, ID# 0718-175, from the puddle along the west side of the pad where the EC is between 7.5 and 8.35 mS/cm, adjacent to the location where the 10H GPU had been staged. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted.

Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported at 2:05pm on Monday, 6/7/2021. The release to the ground occurred as a result of the 4 1/2" casing pressuring up during routine maintenance on the well with a service rig. The 2" tubing was blown down prior to the incident. The estimated volume of oil released to the ground is 30 gallons. Consisting of pooled oil and misted oil around the rig and wellhead and spreading out within the hay field approximately 65-80 feet from the well. Approximately 19 gallons of pooled oil was collected and placed into the production tank. The vegetation (hay) that was covered with the mist of oil was cut down and bagged up for disposal. The majority of the impacted area was scrapped up with an excavator and loaded into a triaxle truck for disposal. Clean fill onsite was being applied to the excavated area as part of the cleanup/reclamation. The cleanup operation will continue Violations cite.

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection on 12/26/2020 found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment had been removed however there was snow and ice partially covering the bottom of the containment. Between this inspection and the last inspection water has collected in the secondary containment from recent precipitation events. Crude oil contamination is evident on the surface of the water and and on the outside of the tanks. An empty 200 gallon tote is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/29/2025
Comments: I received notification from Oil and Gas Management regarding a public report of water being discharged from the Brown #1 well site, it was stated there was an odd smell, there was concern about if it was safe to be discharged. I arrived onsite and found a hose running down hill from a tank battery on Farm Lane that was used to hold presumed fresh water during the recent completion of this well. The well operator was draining the water tank and using it to water their freshly seeded and mulched areas. I used my conductivity probe and determined the water being discharged from the tank was not suitable to be dispersed to the ground as the conductance of the fluid was in excess of 16000S, which is above the allowable limit of 1000S. The operator immediately shut the valve and ceased the discharge. It is estimated over 1 barrel of fluid was released prior to closing the valve. Mr. Branch called to get additional equipment onsite to begin remediating the release. It was advised to get a vac truck for any standing water, and the mini excavator on site to begin soil removal.From the end of the discharge hose, the water ran approximately 35 feet in a westerly direction across a portion of the site, reaching an open earthen drainage ditch, this ditch connects to the local storm sewer somewhere along Crestview Blvd. Flowing water in the storm sewer was observed at the bottom of Crestview Blvd, due to lack of access I was unable to get my conductivity probe into the water to determine if it was from the Brown #1 site.

Comments: Arrived on location in the morning on 11/25/2024 with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 33 degrees. PADEP representatives OGI Thomas Antonishak called Chris McCoy and then met with Brian Reynolds - Operator (Hilcorp) representative onsite to obtain a status of operation activities update. Cementing contractor, American Cementing on site along with Nine wireline. The Operator worked through the weekend on Saturday 11/23/24 and Sunday 11/24/24 - See plugging procedure/plan and cement section(s) of this inspection report for operations summary reported and provided by the operator to OGI, Thomas Antonishak. Currently, rigging up Nine wireline truck, cable, lubricator, bails, and tools. Silence all electronics on location while wireline prepares charges for perforations. Go in hole with wireline to depth of 760' and perforate casing from 760' to 754'. No injection or entry at perforations. Rig down wireline, swap lines, and fill wellbore with fluid, pressure up to 1,500 psi and hold (photo #1). No injection, the wellbore held pressure without any leak off. Go in hole to depth of 775' (photo #2). Mix and pump 3.8 bbl (21 sks) 16.4# cement for perforations from 775' to 725' (50' thick) in 9 5/8". Pull out of hole. Make up 9" cement retainer and run in hole to 705' (photo #3). Mix and pump 11.7 bbl (63 sks) 16.4# cement for surface casing shoe from 705' to 555' (150' thick). Mix and pump cement from 200' to 50' (150' thick) in 13 3/8". Pull out of hole and prepare for rig down of rig and equipment for mobilization. Additional forthcoming activities planned for next week, after the Thanksgiving holiday will include excavating out and around plugged well riser more than 3-feet (plow depth) to then sand aggregate well from 50' to surface, install permanent monument as steel plate placard affixed atop riser with well API welded label, back fill monument to then restore location.

Comments: On April 19, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an investigation of a reported spill (CTS No. 356072) at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported on April 19, 2021, after removing the second AST off the well pad an area of high conductivity and staining was observed in the highly compacted soil where the tank was located. The estimated volume of the spill was about 500 gallons of production fluid. The area of impact was about 120 ft. X 150 ft. circle with varying levels of conductivity. A contractor was onsite beginning to excavate the impacted soils. The contractor was removing about 6 to 8 inches of impacted soil. The area of impact was screened by Beech Resources for conductivity. Areas where the compacted soil had already been removed had a conductivity near 320 uS/cm to 910 uS/cm. Conductivity of areas that had not yet been excavated at the time were around 1.69 mS/cm. There were no seeps off the well pad observed. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect confirmatory samples on April 20, 2021. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection Reports 3139277 and 3141035 still remain.

Comments: Bull Run Resources contacted WQSS Brian Ayers to inform him of a release that occurred overnight on April 16, 2025 their Peterson P9 well, located in Pleasant Twp Warren County. I arrived on site and spoke with Sam Harvey from Bull Run. Sam informed me that the cause of the release was a high pressure stuffing box on the well head failed for an unknown reason. The emergency low pressure switch on the well head also did not function as designed. Production fluid was released from the well head and traveled downslope following a series of road ditches and culvert crossings. The release does not appear to have progressed past a power line located just north of the well. Several underflow dams have been constructed in the ditch lines and are working effectively at this time. Absorbent pads are being used at the siphon dams to collect any production fluid accumulating behind them. The quantity of the release is estimated between one half to one barrel. Bull Run was having roll off dumpsters delivered while I was onsite. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility.Upon completion of the remediation, confirmatory samples are expected to be collected and their results provided to the Department. Documentation verifying the disposal of the impacted soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8181536
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/29/2024
Comments: On 3/29/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected during drilling operations from two different locations at the site.During inspection #3724668 conducted on 3/6/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. On 3/27/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-087 was collected from a channel of water along the north perimeter berm that appeared to have a white substance along the length of it. The water field tested at 4.10 mS conductance. The puddle was near the outfall leading to the sediment basin and was approximately 60 feet long and ranged from 6 inches to 2 feet wide and up to 1.5 inches deep. A 2 inch wide by 1 inch deep stream of water was flowing down the outfall that field tested at 4.11 mS conductance. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The results are shown in pictures 1 and 2. Sample 9551-088 was collected from the sediment basin where a white plume was visible leading into the sediment basin coming from the rock outfall leading off the pad. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin from the pad field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 3 and 4.Noted during inspection #3724668, water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 1.156 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 1.084 mS conductance. During previous inspections, water flowing in a channel below the northeast corner of the pad and below the sediment basin field tested at 0.3 mS conductance or less.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.During inspection 3704886 conducted on 1/29/2023, sample 9551-080 was collected from a channel of water along the northeast cornerof the pad that field tested at 4.2 mS conductance. The laboratory analysis of the sample showed elevated levels of pH, calcium, iron, chlorides and strontium as shown in pictures 5 and 6. Bags of deicing media was reported as being applied near this area.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).This incident has the potential to cause pollution as defined by 25 PA Code 93.6(a), 25 PA Code 93.6(b), and 25 PA Code 91.33(a) and does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b).Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the white substance, elevated conductance, pH, aluminum, iron, and strontium in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

The puddle was near the outfall leading to the sediment basin and was approximately 60 feet long and ranged from 6 inches to 2 feet wide and up to 1.5 inches deep. A 2 inch wide by 1 inch deep stream of water was flowing down the outfall that field tested at 4.11 mS conductance. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The results are shown in pictures 1 and 2. Sample 9551-088 was collected from the sediment basin where a white plume was visible leading into the sediment basin coming from the rock outfall leading off the pad. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin from the pad field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 3 and 4.Noted during inspection #3724668, water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 1.156 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 1.084 mS conductance. During previous inspections, water flowing in a channel below the northeast corner of the pad and below the sediment basin field tested at 0.3 mS conductance or less.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.During inspection 3704886 conducted on 1/29/2023, sample 9551-080 was collected from a channel of water along the northeast cornerof the pad that field tested at 4.2 mS conductance. The laboratory analysis of the sample showed elevated levels of pH, calcium, iron, chlorides and strontium as shown in pictures 5 and 6. Bags of deicing media was reported as being applied near this area.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).This incident has the potential to cause pollution as defined by 25 PA Code 93.6(a), 25 PA Code 93.6(b), and 25 PA Code 91.33(a) and does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b).Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the white substance, elevated conductance, pH, aluminum, iron, and strontium in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/21/2026
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8289169
Permit API: 081-22022
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McHenry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/21/2026
Comments: On September 21, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response site inspection at the EQT ARO LLC COP Tract 027B Pad B. EQT reported to the DEP spill hotline that a water truck hauling produced fluid spilled approximately 100 gallons of produced fluid from a faulty sight glass on the water truck onto the access road of the well pad at 0800. Upon arriving onsite, EQT had delineated the spill on the access road and had that area blocked off from traffic. EQT said that Penn E and R was responding to assist with the investigation and collect confirmatory samples for the ACT 2 process. EQT was investigating how much of the produce fluid had spilled off the road edge. Approximately three areas along the road edge were found to have elevated soil conductivity. One of the areas found was a culvert with produced fluid caught in the outfall. The soil conductivity of the impacted area ranged from 200 uS/cm to over 4,000 uS/cm, which is the upper limit of the DEP soil conductivity meter. The delineated area of impact was approximately 10 feet by 415 feet measure by Penn E and R. While onsite, equipment was delivered to begin the excavation of the impacted area. EQT's contractor began removing the impacted soil from the access road. The contractor scraped the road surface and excavated approximately 4-6 inches of soil off the road edge to removed the impacted soil. Approximately 100 feet of the spill area had been excavated prior to DEP leaving the site. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 401, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted. EQT plans to remediate the spill through the ACT 2 process.

Inspection Date: 8/19/2026
Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

Comments: On Wednesday February 27, 2019 I received notification of a release of produced fluid at the Rogersville/Shumaker Well Site located in Center Township, Greene County. The release was identified and reported to the Department the previous day at approximately 1739 hours. On Wednesday morning I conducted an incident inspection to assess the situation. While on-site, I spoke on the telephone with Mr. Corey Giles from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding details of the release and subsequent remediation. The release occurred as a result of a dump valve wash-out in the GPU associated with the 9H gas well (059-26433). EQT estimated that approximately 14 gallons of produced water was released due to the wash-out. Approximately four (4) gallons of produced fluid remained inside the GPU, while the remaining 10 gallons had exited the unit and impacted soils behind the unit. EQT's remediation contractor was mobilized and the impacted area was remediate. The impacted area was delineated and the completeness of remediation was verified by collecting soil conductivity readings with a portable probe. Due to saturated ground conditions, additional material was removed to ensure all impacted materials were removed. The excavated materials were placed into four (4) 55-gallon drums for off-site disposal and the excavation was backfilled. The release of produced water and impact to soil, as self reported by the operator to the Department, is a violation of 25 Pa. Code Sections 78a.54 and 78a.57(a), and 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 (SWMA 301). The operator should respond in accordance with instructions provided in this notice.
